correctness.rationale: For each reflected pair of arcs, integrating the Fourier coefficient of the indicator gives analytic derivative (4/π)Σ_{n≥1} sin(nδ)cos(nθ)z^(n−1). Summing the geometric series gives numerator Nθ=cosθ(1+z²)−2cz over Qθ, the product of the two quadratic endpoint factors, with the stated prefactor. Adding the pairs gives P=N_a Q_b+N_b Q_a. At an endpoint of the θ-pair, Nθ=−2z sinθ sin(θ±δ)≠0, while Q for the other pair is nonzero. At any non-endpoint boundary point with value 0, the Poisson integral divided by 1−r on the radial approach tends to a strictly positive integral of 2/|e^{iφ}−e^{iθ}|² over the arcs (with normalized angular measure); where the boundary value is 1 use 1−u and the complement instead. Thus there is no unit-circle root of P. The reciprocal identity z⁶P(1/z)=P(z) implies exactly three interior zeros with multiplicity, even when there is a zero at the origin: if its order is m, the degree is 6−m and the remaining 6−2m zeros pair by inversion. Substituting t=z+1/z reduces Qθ/z² to t²−4c cosθ t+4(cos²θ+c²−1) and Nθ/z to cosθ t−2c. The resulting cubic is exactly H. When A+B≠0 there is no zero at the origin and every t outside [−2,2] has a unique inverse strictly inside the disk with nonzero derivative of the forward map. A root in [−2,2] would produce a circle root. Therefore the ordinary real discriminant gives precisely the claimed real versus conjugate-pair alternatives and a real repeated root at zero discriminant. Independent exact integer discriminants: 500H has coefficients (25,360,83,−2961) and (25,−612,110,−1017) for the two witnesses. Dividing their discriminants by 500⁴ gives respectively 14626551073/2500000000 and −914716481579/62500000000. Along A=1/20−B, 3/5≤B≤4/5, the gap a−b increases with B, while b>δ and a<π−δ throughout. At its minimum cos(a−b)=−0.33+0.8√0.6975<0.62=cos(2δ). Hence the sign-changing segment remains admissible and nonantipodal. For a+b=π the boundary indicator is the pullback via w=z² of the two arcs centered at ±2b with half-width 2δ; uniqueness of the harmonic extension gives the same pullback inside. The two-arc derivative has one interior zero solving cos(2b)(1+w²)=2 cos(2δ)w, with |cos(2b)|<cos(2δ). The small root has the stated magnitude and sign; z²=w lifts it and differentiation adds a zero at 0. At b=π/4 that root is simple at w=0 and the pullback derivative has order three at z=0. Thus the imaginary-axis transition applies only to the antipodal subfamily. originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge pass for the explicit equal-width reflected four-arc phase diagram: reduction to a cubic in the geometric parameters, discrimination of real and nonreal phases with a verified nonantipodal collision, and a separate exact antipodal formula. The ordinary Poisson derivative, reciprocal root counting and general critical-point location framework are not credited as new. The leading-coefficient exception must not be evaluated by the cubic test. The inaccessible Walsh texts leave a specific historical risk, not affirmative coverage or clearance.
residual_risks: Walsh's 1947 and 1948 primary theorems and the related chapter of the 1950 monograph were not compared in full. They could contain related locations, a general count, or even more specialized geometry. The related Walsh note found through Project Euclid likewise did not yield full text. No access failure or keyword miss is counted as evidence that these results lack the cubic or its implications.

value.rationale: For the natural equal-width symmetric family the exact classification identifies when all interior saddles remain on the reflection diameter, when a conjugate pair leaves it, and how collisions can occur. The discriminant has realizable strict phases with a collision in the nondegenerate admissible region, rather than merely giving a generic upper bound on the number of critical points. The antipodal formula gives an exact benchmark and isolates a width-independent triple collision. These are useful geometry and decision criteria, not a claim about all level sets or general nonsymmetric four-arc configurations.
